sentence: Japanese farewells hide a similar gap between literal pieces and everyday translation: [sayonara](/sayonara-meaning/) is glossed as a simple "goodbye," but its literal sense is closer to "if that\'s how it is," and unlike a casual arigatō, it signals a long or permanent parting rather than an everyday one.

That kind of register judgment runs through a lot of Japanese social vocabulary, not just this word: [sayonara](/sayonara-meaning/) carries a formality of its own, one tied to finality rather than politeness, and misjudging either word\'s weight reads as off in a similar way.
